description: Create the included private PostgreSQL VM, with PostgreSQL installed automatically. Its fixed size is 1 CPU, 1 GiB RAM and 2 GiB total disk including Ubuntu. Create the included website VM first: all database access, including administration, goes through that website. No direct public SQL, SSH or HTTPS endpoint is provided for this database. No paid or pilot fallback. Create application tables in database redu as role redu, never as postgres. For local administration use sudo -u postgres psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d redu and SET ROLE redu before application DDL or imports. This preserves console read/edit access and its default reader grants. A separate website runtime role may remain read-only. The default pg_hba.conf permits remote login only as redu from the website private address. For a separate runtime role, also add an exact host rule for database redu, that role and the website private IPv4 /32 with scram-sha-256 before the reject rules; validate pg_hba_file_rules and reload PostgreSQL. Keep all other sources rejected; never use trust or a public CIDR. Read the website address from the guest configuration rather than guessing it. SQL grants alone do not permit a new network login. Test the application connection from the website using its actual runtime role, without printing credentials, before publishing. If a shell command returns a nonzero exit code or the app returns HTTP 503, inspect its saved output and sanitized application error; do not repeat the installation blindly. Verify the table through postgres_data_read using the data-view ID returned by get_free_resources; discovery alone does not prove row access. Do not grant superuser or bypass row security to fix a permission error.

request_key.description: Stable request key. Reuse it after a timeout; never repeat an unknown command with a new key.

name: create_free_postgres
